references.text: God creates the firmament (raqia) on the second day, which he names 'heaven' in verse 8.
God gives names to 'the earth' and 'the sea', parallel to the naming of the firmament as 'heaven' in verse 8.
'The heavens declare God's glory; the firmament proclaims the work of his hands' — a hymn pointing back to the creation of the firmament.
'By the word of the Lord were the heavens made' — confirming that the heavens were created by God's word, as described in Genesis 1.
A hymn to God who created the heavens with wisdom and spread out the earth over the waters, consistent with the creation account.
'He who stretches out the heavens like a curtain' — a description of God as the creator of the firmament.
'By his understanding he stretched out the heavens' — God as the creator of the earth and the heavens, parallel to Genesis 1:8.
'By faith we understand that the world was created by the word of God' — a New Testament confirmation of creation by God's word.
Verse 1:8 defines the firmament as heaven, which is necessary context for understanding the placement of the lights on 'the firmament of the heavens' in 1:14.
The connection shows the logical order of creation: first the space (the firmament in 1:8), then its contents (the lights in 1:16).
